column5: deviation. The resolution's drain (`join_next` + `expect` until the set is empty) rests on the premise that every serving task has completed once every child has exited. I ran that literal shape: the inter-process proptest hung on it in roughly one plan in twelve (a 60 s bounded drain expired, so the test failed on `Elapsed`). Instrumented runs (I/O counts on the parent's link plus an EOF-logging wrapper on its control read) show the parked sessions completed their handshake exchange, opened and accepted no data stream, and never observed the control stream's EOF: they wait for a stream the dead child never opens, which the link contract leaves to the caller's timeout. So the wind-down grants this bounded grace, then aborts and joins. The grace is headroom over scheduling latency only; expiring costs sharpness (an aborted session counts as a possible loss), never a false failure. fresh-eyes repair 2: the doc now says the fault-free pin is what holds the grace to its premise.

Under the previous abort-and-discard wind-down this plan passes with the panic only in captured stderr; with panics swallowed in both settle loops it fails with `test did not panic as expected` (output in the commit message).
The probe knob lives on a sibling entry point rather than a `ProcPlan` field so the four reconstructed plans and the strategy stay untouched; `run_proc_plan` delegates with `None`.

The accept loop ends by a stop signal (the resolution's `close the listener rather than abort`): the task returns, dropping the listener, and hands its `JoinSet` back intact so no serving task's outcome is discarded.
Accept ordinal, so the tripwire can target one connection deterministically (children connect sequentially, so accept order is the child's phase order).

deviation, see the `SERVE_GRACE` row: bounded grace drain (with the resolution's `expect`), then `abort_all` on the contract-covered stragglers, then a join of every task that fails on any panic (the resolution's `JoinError::is_panic` alternative). An abort cannot mask a panic that already happened, and a serving task has no panic site after its session returns, so the join is total over panics.

Nit swept: `serve_errors` is read after the serving tasks settle rather than at reap time, so an error landing between the last child's exit and the wind-down is counted; aborted stragglers count too. fresh-eyes repair 2 follows at the next region: the fault-free pin.

Module doc restated as the ruling asks: the Open-time fork is the shadow's model, the live session forks after its preamble exchange (`prior_tree` is taken after `handshake::preamble` in `Rumors::gossip`), and the executor's guard is the consequence of the two forking at different points. I say `once its preamble exchange completes, some polls later` rather than `at its first poll` because with the tiny overlap buffer the fork lands several alternation rounds in; the entry's `first poll` was an approximation.

`Open` doc no longer states the fork as fact; it names the model and the live fork point, and points at the guard. Also notes a `Step` can complete a short session, which the executor already handles.

The named inter-process bound, per connection (each child connection is its own link, so a cut's budget counts that connection alone). fresh-eyes repair 3 re-measured with the two-direction envelope: bootstrap 784, session 1369, final gossip 2194, retire 2750 bytes per endpoint; 3072 sits in the band [2750, 5500]. It equals the intra-process `MAX_CUT` by measurement, not derivation: the two families pin separately.

`arb_child_plan` draws every cut from `MAX_CHILD_CUT`. Committed seeds regenerate through this range (the file's own note on reconstructed counterexamples covers it); no new seed appeared; the reconstructed plans' literal offsets (max 2047) stay below the bound.

fresh-eyes repair 3: the dominance argument is now per direction by set size, and the envelope supplies both directions. A connection moves in one direction at most what its sender holds and its receiver lacks; the real ceilings are the child's own sends plus what it relayed from the other parent peer (child to parent) and the seeds plus the other children's sends (parent to child), stated with the generator's constants. `Envelope::stock` gives every connection after the bootstrap at least both ceilings (the child sends fresh values and relays a complement from the second parent peer; the served peer gains another complement). I chose the set-size argument over a measured floor from the children because the children's exit-code channel cannot carry a byte count and a stdout back-channel would add harness machinery for one number.

Two-sided pin in the shape of `max_cut_spans_the_envelope_session`. negative control: `MAX_CHILD_CUT = 4096` fails the upper side (`is more than twice the child cycle's 1749 bytes`); `= 1` fails the lower side; outputs in the commit message.
`ByteMeter::read` exposes the read counter (the one a `read_cut` spends) so the asymmetric witness places its one-byte-short cut on the same accounting the cut uses, as the meter's doc promises.

The named bound replacing the literal 400. Measured clean fixture: A wrote 188, B wrote 191, B read 188; 256 sits in the band [191, 382]. The literal 400 fails the pin's upper side (more than twice the session), i.e. more than half the old family's cuts landed past the session's end.

The acceptance's deterministic asymmetric case: B's read budget one byte short of a clean session, A `Ok`, B no `Ok` and terminal `Error::Epilogue`, then the full `check_severed` (certification holds). Read cuts join the family on either side (optional, so the always-present write cuts keep their coverage), and the doc claims only what the family produces, pointing at the deterministic witness for the asymmetric case.
